findingsForArchitect: OMP pin content (not a PR defect; the single-source design makes the fix a one-line bump): the image bakes `LEGION_OMP_PATH=/opt/omp/bin/omp` = release 18.1.15-sami.20260908-220934, and every worker the image runs is `legion worker-shim` → `omp --mode rpc`. That release lacks sjawhar/oh-my-pi@0e57a6ca (`fix(rpc): observe extension send rejections when no prompt scope is active` — an extension send that starts no turn crashes a headless rpc session with an unhandled rejection). Verified: raw runtime-init.ts at v18.1.15-sami.20260908-220934, v18.1.15-sami.20260910-172022 and the newest release v18.1.18-sami.20260912-032540 (published 2026-09-12T03:53Z) all contain the pre-fix `send did not invoke the agent` line and none contains `invokingTask.catch(() => {})`; `gh api compare <tag>...0e57a6ca` → diverged, ahead_by=1 for all three; branch fix/rpc-extension-send-rejection still points at 0e57a6ca. The dogfood daemon on this box runs a hand-built `~/.local/state/legion/sjawhar-legion/omp/omp-18.1.15-sami.9bff2014-rpcfix` instead of the pin (this pane's shim cmdline), and LEGION-10 makes the smoke rig do the same via LEGION_OMP_PATH. So the first published image will carry an OMP known to crash headless workers on the path production had to patch. Recommended: land 0e57a6ca on `sami`, cut a fork release, bump OMP_FORK_PIN in omp-pin.ts (one line) before LEGION-24 runs pods from the image — or accept the image as pipeline-proof only until then.

LEGION-12 reproduced in this pane, with a sharper characterisation: the bash tool injects 1–3 `export LEGION_GRANT=` blocks per call (the count varied call to call); only the FIRST injected grant of a call redeems (`legion gh` → real App token; GitHub's own 403 on /user proves redemption), every later one 403s at the daemon (`Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT`) although auth.ts grants are 60 s TTL and not single-use — so the later blocks are minted against something the daemon does not know (a duplicate hook instance?). The implementer's DEBUG-trap workaround did not fire here: the injected preamble is executed without triggering the persistent shell's DEBUG trap (trap -p DEBUG shows it installed; it fires for my own lines). Workaround used: two-call pattern — one call mints, the next call (within the 60 s TTL) hardcodes the previous call's first grant.
